title: THE ROOM MAKER — a brainwave connector that pulls room jobs from the server and renders them with Stable Diffusion
detail:
WHAT: the home box makes the ROOMS — background scenes for Layerz PIXEL (1990s point-and-click adventure rooms, pixel-art) — on request from the server, so every Layerz player draws from one growing pool and a generation only happens when a player has seen every room in it. Elijah's plan (2026-10-20): 'set up Stable Diffusion on my home computer, add a tunnel to my server. Layerz can call the server … it'll only generate after the user has seen all of the options … it keeps adding up across all users.'

WHERE THE PIECES ARE: the SERVER side (the pool, /api/rooms) is filed to ~/repos/elijahlucian.ca/handoff.jsonl as ll-2026-10-20-room-pool (the full HTTP contract); the CLIENT is shipped in waveloop/ios/layerz/Sources/PixelScene.swift (`RoomPool`, base https://elijahlucian.ca/api/rooms). THIS entry is the MAKER: a brainwave connector that turns a queued job into a picture.

THE CONNECTOR — connectors/rooms/rooms_worker.py, registered in config.json under connectors as {"type":"python","script":"connectors/rooms/rooms_worker.py","args":["--server","https://elijahlucian.ca","--backend","a1111"],"description":"Room pool maker: pulls txt2img jobs from the server, runs Stable Diffusion, posts the PNG back","vram_mb":4500} so `bw start rooms` runs it and the VRAM budget knows about it. PULL, NOT A TUNNEL: the worker polls GET {server}/api/rooms/jobs?token=$BRAINWAVE_ROOMS_TOKEN every 5 s (no open ports at home, survives IP changes, the Rust daemon restarts it like any connector); a job is {job, prompt, promptKey, w, h, negative?}. It renders and POSTs multipart {image=png} to {server}/api/rooms/jobs/<job>/done (same token in a header); on failure POST …/failed with a reason. Token: an env var on both ends, never in config.json or git.

THE PICTURE: backend A — AUTOMATIC1111 on :7860, POST /sdapi/v1/txt2img {prompt, negative_prompt, width, height, steps 20-28, cfg 6-7, sampler DPM++ 2M Karras, seed -1}; backend B — ComfyUI (a saved workflow JSON, queue it over :8188/prompt, poll /history); backend C — diffusers in-process (SD 1.5 fp16 ~4 GB; or SDXL-Turbo at 4 steps if the card has room). Size: the job's w×h is the pane in POINTS (e.g. 328×680); render at 2–3× that rounded to a multiple of 64 (768×1024 portrait is the default), portrait, never crop. Style: a pixel-art / LucasArts / 90s adventure-game checkpoint or LoRA if one is on disk, else plain SD with the prompt carrying the style; NEGATIVE: people, person, face, hands, text, watermark, logo, signature, blurry, photo. The app blocks the picture to 8-pt cells and snaps it to a 19-colour palette (steel, walnut, brass, plastic, red, white, teal, ice, orange, lavender) — so composition and lighting matter, fine detail doesn't; dark rooms with warm lamps read best. The default prompt everyone shares: 'a 1990s point-and-click adventure game room, pixel art: a cosy dim music room with wood panels, a brass-framed window, a worn rug and an old tape machine, LucasArts style, wide shot, nobody in it'. A player's own prompt comes through as-is.

RULES: one job at a time; idle the card between jobs (brainwave's idle_timeout); log each job (prompt, seed, seconds) to connectors/rooms/log.jsonl; keep the last 50 PNGs locally for Elijah to look at; never generate when no job is queued (the point of the pool is FEWER generations over time). When it is running, append a `note` here with the first room's job id and the seconds it took, and a `note` in elijahlucian.ca's ll-2026-10-20-room-pool so the server side knows a maker is online. LATER (not now): img2img from the player's actual camera frame as the init image so the room resembles their space; the same worker serving Choppa / Tide / Wake (the job's `app` field).

note:
SIZES, from the client's layout (ios/layerz PixelLayout / StageFace, measured on a 16 Pro, 402×874 pt, safe area 59+34):
PIXEL — the picture is 42×61 cells of 8 pt (336×488 pt; a 15 Pro gives 41×58). Render 704×1024 px PORTRAIT (the nearest multiple-of-64 shape); 512×768 is fine too — the app blocks to 8-pt cells and snaps to 19 colours, so only the SHAPE matters. STAGE (if rooms ever go behind the stage's picture — not wired yet): the picture inside the brass frame is 334×499 pt upright on a phone (ratio 0.67 → 704×1024 as well, a 3% crop either way), ~780×692 pt on an iPad or a wide Mac window (1.13 → 1088×960), ~456×334 pt on a phone sideways (1.37 → 1024×768). STAGE dithers at 2 pt and keeps six levels a channel, so detail shows there — render at 2× the points or more. THE RULE: every job carries the pane's w and h in POINTS; render at that aspect, rounded to multiples of 64, at 2–3× the points, portrait or landscape as given; never crop or letterbox — the app aspect-fills, so a wrong shape loses the edges, not the middle.
